Let me understand the exact overflow scenario. In `fxGetNextTokenJSXChild`:
- `p = parser->buffer` and `q = p + parser->bufferSize - 1` (so q points to the last valid byte)
- Text characters are written via `fxUTF8Buffer` which checks `string + mxStringByteLength(character) > limit` and reports a memory error but still writes.
- When `&` is encountered, `fxGetNextEntity(parser, p, q)` is called.

In `fxGetNextEntity`:
- `*p++ = '&'` - writes unconditionally
- If next char is `#`: `*p++ = '#'` - writes unconditionally
- If next char is `x`: `*p++ = 'x'` - writes unconditionally

So the overflow happens when the buffer is nearly full. If `p` is at `q` (the last valid position), then `*p++ = '&'` writes at `q` (valid), then `p` becomes `q+1`. Then `*p++ = '#'` writes at `q+1` which is **out of bounds** (1 byte overflow). Then `*p++ = 'x'` writes at `q+2` (2 bytes overflow).

In `fxUTF8Buffer`, the check is `string + mxStringByteLength(character) > limit`. So if `string == limit`, then `string + 1 > limit` is true, and it reports a memory error but still writes at `string` (which is `q`, the last valid byte). So after `fxUTF8Buffer` writes at `q`, `p` becomes `q+1`.
